title: Docker
summary: Docker builds images from a Dockerfile and runs services from a Compose file, with context, cache, tag and merge rules an agent must respect.

sections.label: Where config lives
sections.text: Docker reads a file named Dockerfile at the root of the build context unless the build names another file. A .dockerignore in the context root trims the context before it is sent to the builder. Compose looks for compose.yaml, compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml or docker-compose.yml in the working directory and prefers compose.yaml. docker init scaffolds .dockerignore, Dockerfile, compose.yaml and README.Docker.md and offers to overwrite existing files.

sections.label: Conventional commands
sections.text:
# Conventions, not facts about any project. Check its own scripts first.
docker build -t myapp:dev .
docker build --check .
docker compose up --build
docker compose down

sections.label: How CI is declared
sections.text: Docker does not declare a pipeline. Its CI pages present the Dockerfile as a way to define the runtime, operating system and binaries needed to build and test the application in a reproducible container. Docker maintains official GitHub Actions for building, annotating and pushing images and links setup for GitLab, CircleCI and Render.

sections.label: Where review conventions live
sections.text: Build checks inspect the Dockerfile and build options for deviations from current best practices without running the build, and docker build --check reports violations with a non zero exit status. Violations are warnings by default, so to block on them add # check=error=true to the Dockerfile or set the BUILDKIT_DOCKERFILE_CHECK build argument. Checks need Buildx 0.15.0 and Dockerfile 1.8 or later. Other rules are the project's own.

sections.label: Gotchas
items: Everything under the build path except .dockerignore matches reaches the builder and COPY, so node_modules and .git travel unless excluded.
Once a layer changes every later layer is rebuilt, so copy package manifests and install dependencies before the rest of the source.
FROM or a pull without a tag uses latest, tags are mutable, and a pinned digest receives no fixes on its own.
USER sets the user for later RUN steps, ENTRYPOINT and CMD, and Docker recommends a non root user when the service can run without privileges.
Compose merges compose.yaml with compose.override.yaml from the same directory and applies -f files in the order given, later files overriding earlier ones.
The top level version key in a Compose file is obsolete and not used for validation.
Multi stage builds keep build tools out of the final image, and docker build --target stops at a named stage.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting Docker adds the Containerised services profile, which asks about the files a change touches, image pinning, build checks and the runtime user, and does not install Docker, build or verify an image.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the installed Docker and Compose versions, which Compose files and overrides exist, whether build checks run, and whether a project script wraps these conventional commands.

basis: Docker documentation on docs.docker.com read on 2026-10-11, and the Slot 6 deployment target row of the coverage gap research from the same day.
confidence: Documented behaviour has scoped sources that still need review. The command lines are conventions and the review guidance is proposed.

catalog.applicability: Use when a project builds container images from a Dockerfile or runs services with Docker Compose and a coding agent must build, run or review those files.
catalog.limits: Catalogue inclusion does not install Docker, verify a build, or confirm image contents, registry access or runtime behaviour.
